newsitem.title: GERMANY: France not yet fit for EMU - ex-minister Lambsdorff.
newsitem.headline: France not yet fit for EMU - ex-minister Lambsdorff.

text.p: Former German government minister Otto Graf Lambsdorff said on Monday that France looked set to miss the Maastricht treaty's budget deficit target by too much to take part in European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Speaking after an audit found France's budget deficit to be running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product, Lambsdorff told Saarland Radio: "If the numbers stay like this, then France is out."

Lambsdorff added that Paris was overshooting the Maastricht budget deficit target of three percent of GDP "by too much". Since EMU without France was unthinkable, a delay would be "politically desirable", he said.
Lambsdorff, a member of junior coalition partners the Free Democrats, served as Economics Minister from 1977 to 1984.
